item.title: Joining The Dots – Programme 8 Stress & tips to manage it effectively
One in two survey respondents with MS in Wales have been challenged for using accessible facilities
item.description: Almost half (48%) of people surveyed and living with multiple sclerosis (MS) in Wales have been questioned or challenged for using accessible facilities - like Blue Badge parking spaces, accessible toilets and priority seats on public transport – a new survey from leading MS charities has found. To mark this year’s MS Awareness Week campaign, MS Think Again, 90 people living with MS in Wales were surveyed to understand the full impact of public judgements, and to challenge assumptions about MS.

item.title: Community groups receive £10k to support bereavement projects across Wales
item.description: Twenty projects across Wales have received grants of up to £500 to hold events or services that enable communities to support people through grief or ill-health. £10,000 of funding was given to the projects which reached more than 500 people and included group sessions for bereaved children, creative workshops for those grieving the loss of loved ones through suicide and remembrance events for veterans. item.title: Joining the Dots – Programme 5 Neurodiversity Celebration Week; new report on over 60s.
item.description: Under discussion: Neurodiversity Celebration Week, what it is and why it matters. item.title: Joining the Dots – Programme 6 Love your heart
item.description: Our theme is hearts. Yours and mine. Not from a romantic but from a health perspective. We know it’s one of the biggest and most vital organs in the body and yet how many of us look after it in the way we should? I speak to the founder of Calon Hearts, Sharon Owen, about the heart screening her charity provides free to 16-26 year olds.
